name: Cameroun francophone - enseignement secondaire general, 6e a Terminale (BEPC, probatoire et baccalaureat)

sources.title: Decret n°95-035 du 24 fevrier 1995 portant organisation des baccalaureats de l'enseignement secondaire (marks, admission, mentions; read by OCR)
Recueil des textes portant organisation des examens ESG et de l'enseignement technique STT (index of the texts on the examinations; the arretes fixing coefficients per series were not read)

verification.notes: Draft, not reviewed by an officer of the Ministry of Secondary Education or the Office du Baccalaureat. The only rules read from an official text are those of the 1995 decree on the baccalaureates, which concern the examination and not the school year, and which were read from a scanned image by OCR: marks out of 20, the note multiplied by the subject coefficient set by arrete, admission at a moyenne of at least 10 out of 20, and the mentions Passable (from 10, below 12), Assez bien (from 12, below 14), Bien (from 14, below 16) and Tres bien (from 16). The OCR garbled the lower bound of Passable, taken here as 10. Open items: (1) every subject coefficient is 1, a neutral default: the coefficients per series are fixed by arretes that were not read, and the school replaces them (overridable). (2) The school year's internal rules were not found in a fetched official text: the three-trimestre calendar, the annual moyenne (modelled as the mean of the three trimestres, a draft rule) and the promotion threshold of 10 are assumptions from spec 03 Appendix J. The Cameroonian school year may be organised in sequences within the trimestres: not modelled. (3) The probatoire at the end of 1ere and the BEPC at the end of 3e are named as national assessments without their rules. (4) Series (A, C, D, TI, G and the others) are not modelled. (5) Primary education and the Anglophone GCE subsystem are not modelled: a bilingual school needs a separate programme. (6) The optional-test and EPS bonus rules of the decree (only the points above 10 out of 20 count) are not modelled. (7) The moyenne kept to two places and rounded half-up is an assumption. (8) The English labels are a translation of the French; the French labels are drafts no native speaker has reviewed.
